metadata.methods_description: Each trial consisted of a space key press initiation, followed by a fixation dot presentation (500–650 ms duration). Memory encoding phase presented 2 or 6 lateral objects for 1250 ms, with a central cue indicating which object(s) to memorize. The contralateral side displayed irrelevant objects for visual balance. After a 1000 ms delay period, participants performed either a dual task (identifying a same-category distractor object among 4 distractors with accuracy feedback via colored dot) or single task (fixation only). Memory was tested with a two-alternative forced choice probe, where participants selected the cued object using arrow keys, followed by feedback showing the correct object with colored cues. EEG data were preprocessed using standard procedures as detailed in the associated OSF repository.
